title: Test Construction Process and Item Analysis
summary: Steps in test construction; item analysis; item difficulty (p-value); item discrimination; item characteristic curve; item selection; test revision.
revision: Test construction: objectives → item pool → pilot → item analysis → selection → standardisation. p = correct/attempting; optimal p = 0.50.
traps: Test construction: objectives → items → pilot → analysis → selection → standards.
confusions: Believing easier items are always better.

r: Specify what the test will measure.
Generate a large pool of items.
Retain good items; discard poor ones.

notes.t: The proportion of test-takers who answer an item correctly. p = number correct / number attempting.
p ranges from 0 to 1. p = 0.50 indicates maximum discrimination potential. Very easy items (p near 1.0) and very hard items (p near 0.0) discriminate poorly.
The extent to which an item distinguishes high-scoring from low-scoring test-takers.

Worked example: Item difficulty.
40 out of 80 students answer item correctly.
p = 40 / 80 = 0.50.
Interpretation: p = 0.50 — optimal difficulty for discrimination.
Item analysis examines each item's difficulty and discrimination to select items that differentiate between high and low ability while covering the content domain.
UGC NET frequently asks about p = 0.50 as optimal difficulty and the test construction sequence.
